underlying_problems: Coagulant from treatment is leaking into the distribution system as reported by water system users. Testing of treated water showed aluminum from coagulant in excess of the maximum acceptable concentration (MAC). The concentration of the raw water was below the operational guidance level so the aluminum is coming from the treatment. Raw water was 0.0255 mg/L and the treated water is 3.75 mg/L. MAC is 2.9 mg/L Turbidity of the treated water was also elevated and above the 1 NTU required for treated surface water. Treated water was 2.72 NTU. Babies, young children, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers and individuals with kidney complications or on dialysis are at a higher risk of health effects from elevated aluminum. Water system currently on a Water Quality Advisory (WQA) due to operational deficiencies. Underlying problems of the WQA are: 1) One of two Ceramic Ultrafiltration unit (CUF- B) was turned off due to a structural defect. 2) The second CUF unit - A, which serves as the primary treatment barrier for the removal of inorganic and organic constituents, as well as protozoan pathogens such as Giardia and Cryptosporidium, did not meet the requirements of the Indirect Integrity test as stipulated in the permit conditions. 3) The turbidity sensor shut off on the SCADA system used for conducting the Indirect Integrity test is disabled. Turbidity levels in the treated water were observed to exceed 1.06 NTU. 4) The lack of Indirect Integrity Testing, combined with elevated turbidity readings in the treated water, may be indicative of treatment system malfunction
steps_taken_to_remedy: Water system owner will notify the residents of the community about the change from the WQA to a Do Not Consume notice Communication will highlight the vulnerable members of the community Water system owners will provide an alternative drinking water source for those in the community affected by the notice. Northern Health will post the notice on their public drinking water notice page to assist with awareness
corrective_actions_remaining: Test various locations in the distribution system to see if the elevated aluminum and turbidity is consistent throughout the distribution system. Test the output of both CUF units during operation to determine if one or both are leaking coagulant. Have a professional audit the treatment system to find out the source of coagulant leakage. Apply corrective measures to ensure the aluminum operational guideline of 0.1 mg/L is consistently met in the treated water going forward. Perform a visual inspection of the wet well and storage tower looking for coagulant settling on the bottom. Seek out professional advice on cleaning out the coagulant from the distribution system lines. When sample results show a decrease in aluminum in the distribution and the concentration is below the MAC, the Do Not Consume Notice (DNC) can be rescinded and replaced with a Water Quality Advisory. The Water Quality Advisory will retain the non-completed requirements from the DNC (except aluminum above the MAC) and remain in place until the test results show the aluminum is below the operational guidance of 0.1 mg/L Existing requirements of the previous Water Quality will remain as requirements and be added to the DNC but will not need to be met for rescinding the DNC. Those requirements are as follows: 1) Conduct a comprehensive assessment of CUF A in collaboration with the manufacturer or a qualified professional to identify the root cause of the current operational concerns and ensure that the operational malfunctions are addressed such that the CUF unit is working as designed and approved. 2) Operator to identify the cause of elevated levels of turbidity in the treated water. 3) Permeate turbidity levels rgfgthe CUF A must be continuously within the range outlined on the operating permit. Indirect Integrity Testing must be operational, with alarm and shutdown points enabled. 4) Conduct Direct Integrity Testing (DIT) for the CUF A daily and ensure that the results are documented. Provide the results of the DIT to the Environmental Health Officer on a weekly basis for a review.

underlying_problems: The Kitimat water system draws water from the Kitimat River via two infiltration galleries which provide partial filtration for turbidity; however, as the water level in the river rises the effectiveness of the filtration goes down. Snow melt has lead to an increased water level in the river and higher turbidity post infiltration (1.17 NTU). While the water supplier stored clean water when the river level was < 1.8 m, reservoir levels were at the point where dirty water needed to be pumped into the system on the night of May 6 2026 to ensure a sufficient volume is available for fire protection. The turbidity in the system is still >1 NTU as of the morning of May 7 2026. However, the water level has dropped since then and the advisory is expected to remain in place until tomorrow afternoon dependent on turbidity results. The underlying problem for this water system is that there is inadequate treatment of water from the surface water source.
steps_taken_to_remedy: Pump only as much high turbidity water as is necessary into the system and verify a minimum of 0.2 ppm free chlorine can be maintained. If free chlorine cannot be maintained above 0.2 ppm throughout the distribution system or if the water post infiltration goes over 5 NTU, this WQA will likely be upgraded to a Boil Water Notice.
corrective_actions_remaining: Flush dirty water from the system and maintain a minimum 0.2 ppm free chlorine residual and establish a turbidity level of < 1 NTU throughout the distribution system.
